title: Budgeted GPU scheduler: spot/on-demand selection + model-variant fallback policy
creator: Asha Menon
description: Implement a budget-aware GPU routing layer that chooses between spot and on-demand capacity and picks GPU family (A100 / H100 / T4) based on model latency SLOs, per-customer daily budget caps, and graceful fallback to cheaper model variants when cost or capacity constraints trigger. This ticket covers scheduler algorithm, per-tenant budget enforcement, integration points with autoscaler, and telemetry for cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler routes >=95% of requests to cheapest compatible capacity while meeting per-request latency SLOs in synthetic workloads
Per-tenant daily budget caps enforced: requests exceeding soft cap are routed to cheaper variants or throttled according to policy
Fallbacks to smaller model variants produce valid responses and are logged with a trace id for later quality evaluation
End-to-end e2e test demonstrating spot preemption handling and automatic re-routing to on-demand within configured failover window
Dashboard shows cost-saved estimate, spot failure rate, average latency per GPU type, and budget burn-down per tenant
tasks: Design policy DSL for budgeted routing (priority, soft_cap_pct, hard_cap_pct, fallback_chain)
Implement scheduler shim that annotates requests with target GPU-family and capacity type
Integrate with autoscaler to request burst on-demand if preemption spikes and SLA risk is high
Implement per-tenant budget ledger and enforcement hooks
Add tracing and tagging for routed-fallback events
Create e2e tests and load profile simulations
progress_updates: 2026-03-06: Kickoff meeting with infra and product. Agreed on objectives and KPI matrix (cost delta, latency p95, fallback rate).
2026-03-07: Prototype DSL draft posted to Confluence: includes policy fields 'preferred_gpu', 'max_cost_per_krequest', 'fallback_variants'.
2026-03-09: Scheduler shim PoC routes traffic to T4 spot for non-latency-sensitive ops; observed 18% cost reduction in microbenchmarks but increased p95 from 48ms to 78ms for some model versions.

2026-03-11: Design review with PM & SRE. Decision: introduce 'soft_cap_pct' to allow graceful degradation before hard throttles; autoscaler will be allowed to spin on-demand for up to a configurable budgeted burst window.
2026-03-12: Implemented budget ledger prototype and persisted counters. Started wiring fallback event tags into tracing pipeline.
decisions: Use a tiered policy: prefer spot cheapest compatible GPU -> if spot preemption risk high or latency breach predicted, route to on-demand of same family -> if cost exceeds soft cap, route to cheaper model variant -> if hard cap reached, apply rate-limited deny or queue based on tenant policy.
Budget enforcement is per 24h rolling window; soft cap triggers automated fallback but still serves; hard cap enforces strict rate-limits unless override is set by tenant tier.
Fallback variants must be validated by the quality team; fallback chain defined per model in model catalog metadata.
Telemetry for each routed request will include fields: budget_check(reason), selected_capacity, predicted_latency_vs_slo, fallback_chain_step.
tradeoffs: Aggressive spot-first routing yields best cost savings but increases chance of transient latency regressions and complexity handling preemptions.
Allowing autoscaler to burst on-demand reduces customer-visible errors but increases cost and complicates budget guarantees.
Enforcing hard caps simplifies billing predictability for customers but risks API availability; soft caps provide a smoother UX.
Adding per-request predictive latency estimation (ML model) improves routing decisions but requires additional telemetry and compute overhead.
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Park): Ensure fallback QoS labeling so product can report 'degraded' responses in dashboard for end-users.
SRE (Diego Rivera): Add circuit-breaker threshold for repeated preemptions to avoid thrashing the autoscaler.
Design (Maya Li): Provide UX hooks in Console to let tenants preview cost impact of enabling spot-first routing.
Security (Ravi Patel): Confirm that budget ledger data at tenant level is auditable and encrypted at rest.
notes: Next steps: finalize DSL fields, add ML-based latency predictor experiment, and run 48-hour canary for 10 pilot tenants. Coordinate with billing team for cost attribution labels.
